ellie.docs: FYI I opened a docs PR for the rate limits + pricing UX guide. Need a quick pair of eyes before merge — it includes a new SDK snippet for showing token-bucket behavior and a short query for the usage analytics dashboard.

kevin.infra: Thanks — pinged. Which SDK snippet did you add? JS or Python?

ellie.docs: JS first, we can port to Python after. The snippet demonstrates reading X-RateLimit-* headers and falling back to quota tier logic. Pls check the semantics around burst windows.

sam.p: Quick note: the billing team changed the "burst" definition last week — it's now a separate bonus capacity that doesn't decrement the committed quota. Docs should call that out so customers don't think bursts consume their reserved capacity.

ellie.docs: Good catch. I added a short callout section but it's terse. I'll expand to one paragraph. Can you drop the exact phrasing for the PR?

sam.p: Suggestion: "Burst capacity is transient, applied when available to reduce throttling, and is accounted separately from committed quota. Usage shown in dashboards distinguishes burst vs committed tokens"

ellie.docs: Nice — I'll include that. Also uncovered one broken link: the old billing UI path /billing/usage/tiers -> needs to point to /console/billing/usage (internal change).

kevin.infra: For the analytics query — you added a sample SQL for the dashboard widgets? Make sure you namespace by customer_id and model_id to avoid double-counting.

ellie.docs: Yes, here's the snippet I put in the docs section: ```sql
-- tokens per day, by tier
SELECT date_trunc('day', event_time) AS day,
       customer_id,
       usage_tier,
       sum(tokens) AS tokens_used
FROM redwood_usage.events
WHERE event_time >= current_date - interval '30 days'
  AND event_type = 'generation'
GROUP BY day, customer_id, usage_tier
ORDER BY day DESC;
```

alex-sdk: Small nit on the JS SDK snippet: we now expose headers via response.meta.rateLimit in the client. Example should prefer that over raw header parsing. Also show the recommended backoff window (use Retry-After header if present).

ellie.docs: Good call. Current JS snippet (in PR) was this: ```js
// naive example — read headers and decide
const resp = await client.generate({ model: 'redwood-xl', input: '...' });
const headers = resp.headers; // old style
const limit = parseInt(headers['x-rw-ratelimit-limit'] || '0', 10);
const remaining = parseInt(headers['x-rw-ratelimit-remaining'] || '0', 10);
if (remaining < 5) {
  // prefer token-level backoff
  await sleep(500);
}
```

alex-sdk: Replace with: ```js
const { result, meta } = await client.generate({ model: 'redwood-xl', input: '...' });
const rl = meta?.rateLimit || {};
// rl = { limit: 600, remaining: 120, resetSeconds: 22, burstUsed: 0 }
if (rl.remaining < 10) {
  // jittered backoff recommended
  await sleep(Math.random() * rl.resetSeconds * 1000 + 100);
}
```

ellie.docs: I'll swap that in. Also adding a note that burstUsed may appear as a separate field.

ci-bot: build/ci - docs-pr-456 passed (lint ok, linkcheck found 1 broken link: /billing/usage/tiers).

ellie.docs: Thanks CI. I'll update the link and push.

nora.pm: Quick product check — in the pricing table we list "Tier A: 100k committed tokens" — can you also add the per-token price and a link to the pricing calculator? Otherwise customers ask for unit economics.

ellie.docs: Will add a small table row and the calculator link (https://console.redwood.ai/pricing/calculator). Any objections to including a short example cost calc? e.g., 100k tokens * $0.0004 = $40?

sam.p: Helpful, yes. Also add a sentence about metering granularity: we meter at model-call granularity and report both input/output tokens.

ellie.docs: Added both points. Final ask: who can do a fast review for accuracy on the infra bits (burst semantics + headers) so I can merge before end-of-day?

kevin.infra: I can review in ~30m.

alex-sdk: I can LGTM the SDK example after ellie updates it.

ellie.docs: Thanks all. I'll push the fix for the link and the SDK change now, pinging reviewers when done. :pray: 

kevin.infra: thx — if you want, add a small note in the changelog (docs changelog) called "rate-limits: clarify burst vs committed quota" so integrators see the change in release notes.

ellie.docs: Good idea — added to PR description.

alex-sdk: One last note: add a one-line migration snippet for customers using old header names (x-rw-rate-limit-*) -> new meta.rateLimit to avoid surprises.

ellie.docs: will do. planning to merge once CI linkcheck is green.

ci-bot: build/ci - docs-pr-456 linkcheck fixed, all checks passed.

ellie.docs: Merged. Thanks everyone! :tada:
